[...] Kambaata’s stress is morphological, which means that it is primarily used to distinguish between grammatical word forms of the same lexeme. Stress-minimal pairs are easily encountered in any text; compare the nominal minimal pair bírikk (nominative) vs. biríkk (accusative) in (5) and (6), and a verbal minimal pair yéenno (main verb form) vs. yeennó (relative verb form) in (5) and (7). new_statements.rule_in_words: One stress per word; its position is not phonologically fixed but assigned by the inflectional morphology: roots and derivational suffixes are stressless, each inflectional suffix (case/gender on nouns, aspect/mood/dependency on verbs) carries a stress specification realized on itself, on a preceding syllable, on a following syllable, or at the word's right edge (e.g. F.NOM -´a > lókkanne, F.ACC -á > lokkánne, F.GEN -a´# > lokkanné); a few post-inflectional suffixes (jussive negator -´ka, relative suprafix -´#) override it. Only ideophones and interjections have lexical, unpredictable stress (mostly final, some penultimate). Corroborated in print by Treis 2024:157: 'Kambaata is a language with phonemic stress whose position in a word is predominantly grammatically determined.'
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; words normally have a single stress, except that a host plus a case-marked enclitic may carry two stresses (stress behaviour of enclitics flagged by the author as not yet clear, fn. 16).
new_statements.exceptions: Ideophones and interjections have lexically determined stress; enclitic-hosting words may have two stresses; realization of 1SG/3M perfect pre-stressing blocked by a consonant cluster (§5.2.5.3); stress of the long negative imperative 'not yet safely determined'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (grammatical word incl. post-inflectional suffixes); examples drawn from a conversational corpus and elicited paradigms; stress marked with acute accent on orthographic forms. Official orthography does not mark stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Treis describes Kambaata proper (kamb1316, Kambaata-Xambaaro zone, based on speakers from the Kambaata area; official Roman orthography with added acute-accent stress marks). Orkaydo 2021 describes the T'ambaaro/Timbaro variety (Glottolog dialect timb1252 under kamb1316) and gives no placement rule, only 'seems a pitch-accent language'. Glottolog's ref list for kamb1316 also mixes in K'abeena/Qebena works (Crass 2005 etc.), which concern Alaba-K'abeena (alab1254), not Kambaata proper.

sources.note: Every word has exactly one stressed syllable; stress is morphological: roots and derivational suffixes are stressless, inflectional suffixes are stress-determining (stress realized on the suffix, on a preceding syllable, a following syllable, or word-finally), post-inflectional suffixes are stress-neutral or stress-changing; only ideophones and interjections have lexical (unpredictable) stress; countless grammatical minimal pairs (bírikk NOM vs biríkk ACC).

sources.citation: Treis, Yvonne. 2024. Ideophones in Kambaata (Cushitic): Grammar, meaning and use. Linguistic Typology at the Crossroads 4(1): 147-200. doi:10.6092/issn.2785-0943/16393. Sec. 3.2, p. 157.
sources.note: 'Kambaata is a language with phonemic stress whose position in a word is predominantly grammatically determined'; roots undetermined for stress, all inflectional morphemes realized by suffix + specific stress position; minimal pair bóos-u (M.NOM) vs boos-ú (M.ACC); ideophones/interjections have lexically determined stress, mostly ultimate, some penultimate, no antepenultimate.
